concepts.title: Billing an Order at the Restaurant
concepts.definition: The restaurant automation project asks for a kiosk that takes item codes and quantities, computes each line's cost as unit price times quantity, adds the lines into a bill amount, and stamps every bill with a unique order number that restarts at 1 each day.
concepts.key_idea: Combining the date with the per-day order number makes every saved bill uniquely identifiable.
question_patterns: A customer orders 3 plates at 120 each and 2 juices at 60 each. Compute the bill amount.
Why should the order number restart from 1 every day, and how does the bill stay unique?
Which two login types does the restaurant application provide, and for whom?
Write the steps your program follows to turn item codes and quantities into a printed bill.
Which reports should the manager login be able to generate in the order processing project?

solution_steps.explain: Unit price times quantity for the first line.
The same multiplication for the second line.
The bill amount adds every line's cost.

worked_examples.q: A kiosk bills price 120 with quantity 3, and price 60 with quantity 2. What is the bill amount in rupees?

concepts.title: Time Frame for Project Modules
concepts.definition: Every project needs a time frame: estimate each module's duration, multiply by the number of modules, and add the integration and review time so the plan stays structured yet flexible.
concepts.key_idea: A plan without a time frame cannot be monitored, so fixing durations is part of defining the plan.
question_patterns: A project has 4 modules of 6 days each plus 4 days of integration. Compute the total duration.
Why must a project fix a time frame before processing begins?
Three modules take 5 days each and testing takes 3 days. How long does the project run?
Who monitors the project, and from where can a stuck team seek guidance?
What happens to the schedule if one module overruns its estimated days?

solution_steps.explain: Module count times days per module.
Joining the module outputs also consumes days.

worked_examples.q: Four modules take 5 days each and integration needs 4 more days. What is the total project time in days?

concepts.title: Steps in Project Based Learning
concepts.definition: Project based learning moves through five steps shown in Figure 13.1: identify the project from a real-life situation, define a plan with roles for the leader and members, fix a time frame and process, take guidance and monitoring from the teacher, and finally study the single or multiple outcomes, refining them from peer feedback.
concepts.formula: identify -> plan -> time frame -> guide and monitor -> outcome
concepts.key_idea: Each module gets a well-defined task with its own inputs and outputs before integration.
question_patterns: List the steps involved in project based learning in the correct order.
Why should a project idea come from a real-life situation?
What roles do the project leader and the guide teacher play during monitoring?
How does peer review improve the outcome of a project?
Why are interdisciplinary projects encouraged?

solution_steps.explain: Identify the idea, plan roles and tools, fix the schedule, keep gathering guidance while monitoring progress, and evaluate the outcome against feedback.

worked_examples.q: What is the first step of project based learning: identify the project or integrate modules?

concepts.title: Modular, Top Down and Bottom Up Approaches
concepts.definition: A structured or modular approach cuts a project into manageable modules, each with a defined task, inputs and outputs, whose integration produces the final result; a top down approach starts from the whole and splits downwards, while a bottom up approach builds from small parts upwards.
concepts.key_idea: Well-defined module boundaries let different members work independently before integration.
question_patterns: What does a modular approach to a project mean?
Differentiate the top down approach from the bottom up approach.
Why does every module need its own set of inputs and defined outputs?
How does dividing a problem into small modules help a team?
Which approach starts coding from the smallest helpers and builds upward?

solution_steps.explain: Splitting the whole into parts is top down, assembling parts into the whole is bottom up, and both rely on modular boundaries with clear inputs and outputs.

worked_examples.q: Which approach starts from the whole and splits downwards?

concepts.title: Components of Teamwork
concepts.definition: Teamwork is the collective effort of individuals to accomplish a task; its components are communicating with others, listening to others, sharing expertise and tools, respecting every member's views, helping others, and participating actively in discussions.
concepts.formula: teamwork = communicate + listen + share + respect + help + participate
concepts.key_idea: A cricket win needs batting, bowling and fielding together, exactly like project members sharing one goal.
question_patterns: Define teamwork and list its components.
Why must the views of every member be respected in group meetings?
How does sharing expertise help the team finish within the time frame?
Give a sports example that shows why collective effort matters.
Which channels can team members use to communicate with each other?

solution_steps.explain: A team works when members talk, listen, share, respect, help and participate; missing any one weakens the collective outcome.

worked_examples.q: How many components does the chapter list for teamwork: communicating, listening, sharing, respecting, helping and participating?

concepts.title: Project Ideas: Puzzle and Educational Games
concepts.definition: Two sample projects exercise the learned ideas: a grid puzzle where the player clears cells around hidden bombs using number clues on a fixed 6x6 board with 6 bombs, and an edutainment game where a list of 15 cells slides digits rightwards and removes digits that sum to 10.
concepts.formula: clear cells using clue = count of bombs in adjacent cells
concepts.key_idea: New digits enter at the right end and push the existing digits one cell left, so the list behaves like a shifting window.
question_patterns: Describe the clue a cleared cell shows in the bomb puzzle, and how the player uses it.
What grid size and bomb count does the chapter suggest to keep the puzzle simple?
In the Match the Sum game, what happens to the digits when a pair summing to 10 is removed?
Why should both games handle exceptions while the user plays?
How do digits move through the list of cells as new ones are generated?

solution_steps.action: translate the game rule into logic
solution_steps.explain: For the puzzle, count bombs around each clicked cell for its clue; for the sum game, scan the sliding cells for two or three digits adding to 10 and delete them, shifting the rest.

worked_examples.q: The sample puzzle runs on a fixed board of which size: 6x6 or 9x9?

worked_examples.title: Bill for a two-item order
worked_examples.problem: At the Stay Healthy kiosk a customer orders 3 plates at 120 each and 2 juices at 60 each. Compute the bill the program prints.
worked_examples.answer_note: The bill shows 360 plus 120, that is 480, stamped with the day's order number.

worked_examples.title: Scheduling a four-module project
worked_examples.problem: A team plans 4 modules needing 6 days each, plus 4 days to integrate and test. Compute the project's total duration.

steps.explain: Integration and testing take 4 more days.

worked_examples.answer_note: The team should plan for 28 working days in total.

exercises.source_ref: NCERT Class 12 Computer Science, Chapter 13 (in-text activities reworded)
questions: List the five steps of project based learning shown in Figure 13.1 and explain any two.
Explain the modular approach and contrast it with the bottom up approach.
Name the six components of teamwork and describe how sharing helps meet the time frame.
For the restaurant project, design the bill's unique identification and explain why the order number resets daily.
For the bomb puzzle on a 6x6 grid with 6 bombs, describe the clue shown when a safe cell is opened.
For the Match the Sum game, state the rule that removes digits and the condition that ends the game.
Compute the duration of a 5-module project with 4 days per module and 5 days of integration.
A kiosk order has 2 burgers at 90 each and 1 salad at 75. Compute the bill amount.
